officers.name: Daniel Bustos
bio: Daniel is a third-year Electrical Engineering student at UCCS, U.S. Army veteran, and President of the Wire Lion Engineering Club. His interests include power systems, electronics, embedded systems, and hands-on engineering projects that turn concepts learned in the classroom into practical experience.

As president, Daniel is passionate about creating opportunities for students to build projects, develop technical skills, network with professional engineers, and gain experience outside of the classroom. His goal with Wire Lion is to create an environment where students at any experience level can get involved, learn from one another, make mistakes, and develop the confidence to tackle increasingly challenging projects.
For Daniel, engineering is not just about earning a degree; it's about building something, figuring out why it did not work the first time, and working together until it does.

officers.name: Lerry Lara
bio: Lerry is an aerospace engineering student at the University of Colorado Colorado Springs with a strong interest in electronics, technology, and hands-on projects. Through the Wire Lion Engineering Club, Lerry enjoys developing practical skills, collaborating with others, and building projects that prepare students for future internships and careers. The goal is to keep expanding technical knowledge and gain experience in aerospace and engineering-related fields.

officers.name: Kaeden Wellman
bio: Kaeden is a first-year Electrical Engineering student at UCCS, a Division II hurdler on the track and field team, and an officer of the Wire Lion Engineering Club. His interests include embedded systems, electronics, and web development, especially projects where hardware and software have to work together. He has kept a notebook of invention ideas since he was a kid and taught himself web development, app development, and 3D rendering to start building them, including a motion-controlled lightsaber game that streams sensor data from a CircuitPython board into a browser.

At Wire Lion, Kaeden served as project lead on a four-way traffic light intersection, wired and coded on an Arduino to run a full red, yellow, and green cycle. He is also the designer and developer behind this website, wire animation included. He wants Wire Lion to be a place where students show up with an idea, find people to build it with, and walk away having made something real.

For Kaeden, the best part of engineering is watching an idea leave the page. Plenty of the sketches in his invention notebook started as a few lines and a question mark, and engineering is what turns them into a circuit you can wire, code you can run, and a device you can pick up and hand to someone else. He is happiest at the moment a project stops being something he can only describe and becomes something people can actually see, touch, and use.

officers.name: Lakshita Kabade
bio: Lakshita is a freshman at UCCS majoring in Electrical Engineering with a minor in Computer Science, with interests in chip design, embedded systems, hardware security, and SoC design.

Outside of engineering, Lakshita loves dancing, weightlifting, and making content, and is excited to showcase what the club is up to and bring the Wire Lion engineering community to life on social media.

officers.name: William McGinley
bio: Billy is a senior Electrical Engineering student at UCCS with a passion for understanding how things work and turning ideas into real, working projects. His interests range from power systems to electronics, with a particular appreciation for hands-on projects that involve designing, building, testing, and troubleshooting from the ground up.

As an officer of the Wire Lion Engineering Club, Billy enjoys working alongside other students, sharing knowledge, and taking on projects that challenge the team to learn new skills. For him, engineering is about curiosity, creativity, collaboration, and, most importantly, having fun while building something cool.

advisors.name: Leslie Tekamp
bio: Leslie (Les) Tekamp is a Teaching Professor in the UCCS Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering and serves as the faculty advisor for the Wire Lion Engineering Club.
He teaches courses including ECE 2021 Computer-Based Modeling in C, ECE 3610 Engineering Probability and Statistics, and CS 2060 Programming with C.
